Create tools for running retained agents in the background

Source: R/background-tasks.R
background_tools.Rd

Lets owner's model start tasks on retained agents and keep working while they run. The model gets five tools:

Usage

background_tools(
  owner,
  agents,
  usage_limits,
  descriptions = NULL,
  max_active = 4L,
  max_tasks = 16L
)

Arguments

owner

The Agent whose model gets the tools. Register them on this agent only. It can't be a member of, or the owner of, a delegation graph, and can't have a TrustedResults policy.

agents

A named character vector or list of handles from adopt_chat() or owner$retain_agent(). The names are what the model calls the agents.

usage_limits

UsageLimits for each task. A task also can't exceed the agent's remaining budget or the owner run's.

descriptions

Optional named character vector telling the model what each agent is for.

max_active

Maximum number of tasks waiting or running at once. Further starts are refused until one finishes.

max_tasks

Maximum number of tasks in one run of owner.

Value

A named list of ellmer tools for owner$register_tools().

Details

  • task_start(agent, task) starts a task and returns a task ID at once.

  • task_status(task_ids) reports each task's state and progress.

  • task_wait(task_ids, until) waits until a task finishes and returns the finished tasks' outcomes. It makes no model request while it waits.

  • task_follow_up(task_id, task) sends another task to the same agent, which keeps its conversation.

  • task_cancel(task_id, reason) asks a task to stop.

Each task is a call to a retained agent, like owner$continue_agent(): the agent keeps its own permissions, each of its tool calls is also checked against the owner's current permissions and tool hooks, and its work can be followed with owner$observe_subagents() and owner$inspect_subagents(). An agent runs one task at a time, so a task for a busy agent waits its turn.

Tasks belong to the run that started them. When the owner's model stops, tasks that are still waiting or running are cancelled and the run waits for them to stop, so its usage includes theirs. Use owner$background_tasks() to see every task of the latest run, including ones the model never collected.

Use delegation_tool() instead when the model should simply wait for the agent's answer, and a LeadAgent's $parallel_delegate() for one reply each from several subagents with no tools. See vignette("background-tasks").

Budgets

Each task's usage_limits are set aside from the owner's run when the task starts and returned, less what the task used, when it finishes. The owner's own requests and tool calls can't use what is set aside, so together they stay within the run's request and tool-call limits. A task that would leave the owner nothing under one of its run's limits is refused, so give usage_limits a value for each limit the owner's run has. Token and cost limits are checked after each response, so the owner and each running task can each overshoot them by one response.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
lead <- Agent$new(ellmer::chat("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"))
analyst <- adopt_chat(
  ellmer::chat("openai/gpt-6-luna"),
  owner = lead,
  permissions = permissions_readonly(),
  usage_limits = UsageLimits(max_requests = 20),
  history = "fresh",
  callbacks = "replace",
  name = "analyst"
)
lead$register_tools(background_tools(
  lead,
  agents = c(analyst = analyst),
  usage_limits = UsageLimits(max_requests = 5)
))
} # }
